definition: Tabnine is a code completion tool which uses generative artificial intelligence to assist users by autocompleting code.
details: It was created in 2018 by Jacob Jackson, a student at the University of Waterloo. It is now developed by Tabnine, a software company founded under the name Codota by Dror Weiss and Eran Yahav in Tel Aviv, Israel, in 2013, and renamed to Tabnine in 2021. Initially established under the name Codota, the company underwent a rebranding in May 2021 following the release of the company’s first large language model based AI coding assistant, adopting the name Tabnine.

explainer.lead: Tabnine is a code completion tool that uses generative AI to autocomplete code for users. It matters as one of the early commercial AI coding assistants.

tiers.eli5: Like a helpful autocomplete that guesses the next lines of your program as you type.
tiers.practitioner: Developers plug it into their editor to get inline completions; the pitfall is that suggestions must still be reviewed since they are generated, not verified.
tiers.paperLevel: A generative-AI code completion tool; no formal definition or limit is given.

explainer.example: While typing a function signature, the user receives an automatically completed body from the tool.
